newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Japan market seen buoying Australian wool.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Japan market seen buoying Australian wool.

text.p: The sluggish wool pipeline in Japan, a major consumer of Australian wool, at last appeared to be moving, pastoral house Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd said.
Stocks of tops, yarn and fabric in Japan were reduced substantially in the first two quarters of 1996 to normal levels in June, it said in its Wool Watch monthly.
Orders were still below average and stocks had grown slightly since June, but the pipeline situation is definitely more favourable than the same time last year, Wesfarmers said.
The improvement in demand may reflect higher spending power, with disposable income for wage earners in August 2.6 percent ahead of the previous year.
General economic conditions also looked more positive, it said.
In a growing retail consumption market, stocks of greasy and processed wool had been reduced and demand for fresh wool had picked up, it said.
August exports of Australian wool were 16 percent higher than in the same month last year.

On wool prices, Wesfarmers Dalgety said the market over the next month was expected to be driven by the volume of wool available for sale, with large quantities rostered averaging about 100,000 bales a week.
This would limit any upturn in prices, especially for the fine to medium micron category, it said.
If prices did fall, higher pass-in rates, particularly from medium to broad wool growers, was likely to prevent the market falling far beyond current levels, it said.
"The outlook is for prices to fluctuate within a narrow band, but with a greater likelihood of downward movement in the fine wool market," it said.
Wesfarmers also noted that 43 percent more Australian wool was sold at auction between July and the last week of October against the same period in 1995, an increase of 305,000 bales.
This was despite a decline in production this season.
Pass-in rates were much lower than last year, it said.
But the main increase in supply was expected to be coming from wool stored on-farm now coming to sale, it said.
